title: Mobile First Design
definition: A design strategy where you write the default CSS for mobile screens first, and then use `@media (min-width: ...)` queries to add complexity as the screen gets wider.
simpleExplanation: Instead of building a massive desktop site and then struggling to crush it down to fit on a phone (Desktop-First), you start by building a clean, simple phone layout. Then you say: 'Hey, if the screen is big enough (min-width: 1024px), let's add a sidebar'.
realWorldExample: Every modern CSS framework (like Tailwind CSS and Bootstrap) uses Mobile-First architecture because mobile devices account for over 60% of all web traffic.

basic: Which media query is used for Mobile-First: `min-width` or `max-width`?
intermediate: Why is Mobile-First better for performance?

answers.question: Why better for performance?
answers.answer: Phones have slower processors and weaker internet. If you use Desktop-First, the phone has to download all the heavy desktop CSS, process it, hit the `max-width` media query, and then un-do the CSS to make it fit. With Mobile-First, the phone only processes the simple default CSS and ignores the `min-width` desktop queries entirely.
